title: GitHub trend: Uber open-sources detection tools for risky AI agents
friendlyTitle: Uber shares tools for watching and testing AI agent security
summary: Uber's Agentic AI Detection and Response project captures agent intent and tool traces, benchmarks defenses across more than 300 tasks and 133 MCP servers, and detects suspicious sessions. Uber says the system is deployed in production, while the open release includes its sensor, benchmark, and detector rather than its prevention component.
friendlySummary: ADR records what AI agents do and tests whether security systems can notice dangerous behavior. Some prevention features are not open source yet.
whyItMatters: Security teams can use ADR to normalize telemetry from tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex, reproduce agent-security evaluations, and test detection approaches against prompt injection and unsafe tool use. Note that active prevention is not part of the current repository.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use it to study agent activity, test defenses, and find risky actions before using agents widely at work.
